findings.claim: Every DB-clock comparison mixes `clock_timestamp()` (timestamptz) with `TIMESTAMP(3)` (without time zone) columns/variables, so the whole TTL, expiry-ownership and late-consume-becomes-expired contract silently depends on the server's `TimeZone` GUC being UTC: on a non-UTC database inserts always fail closed, and if the GUC has a negative offset the guard accepts a post-deadline consume for |offset| hours instead of writing the required expired tombstone.
findings.reproduction: On a database migrated with this change, in psql: (a) `SET TIME ZONE 'America/New_York'; INSERT INTO "PromptRefinerReservation"("id","stageId","requestId","contractDigest","status","reservedCostMicroUsd","createdAt","expiresAt","updatedAt") VALUES ('tz_probe','prompt-refiner-shadow-v1','tz_probe','sha256:c5cc412eb47821d56f6eed2e837d11086a9ab744069715e90d33ea37a378d55f','reserved',24916,(clock_timestamp() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'),(clock_timestamp() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')+INTERVAL '5 minutes',(clock_timestamp() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'));` — these are exactly the naive-UTC values Prisma writes for `timestamp` columns, yet it raises `PromptRefinerReservation contract binding is invalid`; repeating it after `SET TIME ZONE 'UTC'` succeeds. (b) With a row inserted under UTC whose `expiresAt` is one hour in the past, run `SET TIME ZONE 'America/New_York'; UPDATE "PromptRefinerReservation" SET "status"='consumed' WHERE "id"='tz_probe';` and observe `status='consumed'` with a shifted `consumedAt` instead of the expired tombstone the same statement produces under `SET TIME ZONE 'UTC'`. Fix: write `clock_timestamp() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'` at those five sites. Non-blocking because the repo already assumes a UTC server everywhere (Prisma's own `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` on `TIMESTAMP(3)` columns has the identical dependence), and on the reviewed UTC configuration every criterion holds.
findings.note: Recorded as hardening; no completion criterion is violated on a UTC database.

findings.claim: The doc comment says "Expires active rows in bounded batches", but the `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` has no `LIMIT`: it locks every `reserved` row for the stage and `limit` is only applied by `.slice()` after the client-side filter, so `limit` bounds the writes but not the lock footprint.
findings.reproduction: Call `expirePromptRefinerReservations({ limit: 1 })` with 100 reserved rows present and observe in `pg_locks` that 100 tuple locks are held, not 1. Harmless here because the table is capped at 100 rows; either push `LIMIT`/`expiresAt <= clock_timestamp()` into the SQL or soften the comment.

verdict.nextAction: Approve as-is for the reviewed UTC deployment; optionally apply the `AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'` hardening to the five clock sites in a follow-up before any stage seed exists.
